title: Towards Highly Compatible I/O-Aware Workflow Scheduling on HPC Systems
problem: Scientific workflows on HPC systems require efficient co-scheduling of computing and I/O resources, but existing solutions lack both co-scheduling capability and compatibility with traditional HPC batch schedulers.
motivation: Efficient resource scheduling across workflow tasks with dependencies is crucial for optimizing performance in large-scale HPC systems.
method: The approach builds a performance model to predict how efficiently a scientific workflow will run. THman, an open-source scheduler, uses the Highest Contribution First (HCF) heuristic—a decision rule that prioritizes whichever computing or storage task will make the biggest difference to overall speed. THman makes these scheduling decisions in real-time while coordinating both computing resources and multi-tier storage systems (different storage layers optimized for different speeds and costs), and it integrates with existing HPC batch schedulers so it doesn't require replacing systems already in place.
key_novelty: THman jointly schedules when computing and storage tasks run (co-scheduling) while still working within existing HPC batch schedulers instead of replacing them.
contributions: Performance model for understanding workflow scheduling on HPC systems
THman open-source scientific workflow scheduler with online co-scheduling
Highest Contribution First (HCF) heuristic scheduling algorithm
30.9% makespan reduction demonstrated on simulated and real-world workloads
